$comment: Block format parity: the logical cases and the values the NATIVE CORE produces for them. The expected values are generated by the core — `cargo run -p memphis-core --example emit_block_format_parity` — and are checked by BOTH arms: crates/memphis-core/tests/block_format_parity.rs (native) and tests/unit/block-format-parity.test.ts (TypeScript). If the two arms ever disagree about the bytes or the hash of a block, one of the two tests fails. Do not hand-edit the expected values: regenerate them with the core.

cases.name: plain
cases.why: the baseline: three canonical fields and nothing else.

data.content: a block with fields the hash does not cover

expected_payload.content: a block with fields the hash does not cover

cases.name: extra-fields
cases.why: the hash ignores the fields the contract does not cover; the file keeps them.

data.content: the keys of this payload are not in alphabetical order

expected_payload.content: the keys of this payload are not in alphabetical order

cases.name: mixed-case-keys
cases.why: the keys are sorted BY BYTE, not by locale: `Bravo`, `Zebra`, `apple` — a locale-aware sort would put `apple` first, and the two arms would write different bytes.

cases.name: no-content
cases.why: the fallback branch: a payload with no string `content` gets the canonical JSON of the payload as its content. The two arms used to disagree here — one kept the payload's key order, the other sorted it.

data.content:
zażółć gęślą jaźń — emoji 🎯, a quote ", a backslash \, and
a newline

expected_payload.content:
zażółć gęślą jaźń — emoji 🎯, a quote ", a backslash \, and
a newline

cases.name: unicode-content
cases.why: the bytes where two JSON writers are most likely to disagree: non-ASCII, an emoji, a quote, a backslash and a newline.

data.content: a block that carries the legacy type alias

expected_payload.content: a block that carries the legacy type alias

cases.name: legacy-block-type
cases.why: the type fallback: `type`, then the legacy `block_type`, then `journal`. The native core has always read `block_type`; the TypeScript storage copies did not.
